landmarks.name: Borobudur Temple
landmarks.writeup: A 9th-century Mahayana Buddhist temple in Central Java, known for its intricate stone carvings and massive stupa.

wiki.extract: Borobudur, also transcribed Barabudur, is a 9th-century Mahayana Buddhist temple in Magelang Regency, near the town of Muntilan, northwest of the city of Yogyakarta, in Central Java, Indonesia.

landmarks.name: Komodo National Park
landmarks.writeup: Home to the Komodo dragon, the world's largest lizard, this park encompasses several islands with rich marine biodiversity.

wiki.extract: Komodo National Park is a national park in Indonesia within the Lesser Sunda Islands in the border region between the provinces of East Nusa Tenggara and West Nusa Tenggara. The park includes the three larger islands—Komodo, Padar and Rinca—and 26 smaller ones, with a total area of 1,733 km2 (669 sq mi), with 603 km2 (233 sq mi) of it land. The park was founded in 1980 to protect the Komodo dragon, the world's largest lizard. Later it was dedicated to protecting other species, including marine species. In 1991 the park was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a Man and Biosphere Reserve. It is considered one of the world's 25 biodiversity hotspots.

landmarks.name: Prambanan Temple
landmarks.writeup: A 9th-century Hindu temple complex in Central Java, famous for its tall and pointed architecture dedicated to the Trimurti.

wiki.extract: Prambanan is a 9th-century Hindu temple compound in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, in southern Java, Indonesia, dedicated to the Trimūrti, the expression of God as the Creator (Brahma), the Preserver (Vishnu) and the Destroyer (Shiva). The temple compound is located approximately 17 kilometres (11 mi) northeast of the city of Yogyakarta on the boundary between Central Java and Yogyakarta provinces.

landmarks.name: Raja Ampat Islands
landmarks.writeup: An archipelago in West Papua known for its stunning coral reefs and diverse marine life, popular for diving.

wiki.extract: Raja Ampat, or the Four Kings, is an archipelago located off the northwest tip of Bird's Head Peninsula, Southwest Papua province, Indonesia. It comprises over 1,500 small islands, cays, and shoals around the four main islands of Misool, Salawati, Batanta, and Waigeo, and the smaller island of Kofiau.

landmarks.name: Mount Bromo
landmarks.writeup: An active volcano in East Java, famous for its scenic sunrise views and cultural significance to local Tenggerese people.

wiki.extract: The Bromo, or Mount Bromo, is an active somma volcano, a Hindu pilgrimage site, and part of the Tengger mountains, in East Java, Indonesia. At 2,329 meters (7,641 ft), it is not the highest peak of the massif, but is the most active and famous. The area is one of the most visited tourist destinations in East Java, and the volcano is included in the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park. The name Bromo comes from the Javanese pronunciation of Brahma, the Hindu god of creation. At the mouth of the crater, there is an idol of Ganesha, the Hindu god of wisdom, which is worshipped by Javanese Hindus. Mount Bromo is located in the middle of a plain called "Sea of Sand", a nature reserve that has been protected since 1919.

cultural_events.name: Nyepi Day
cultural_events.writeup: Balinese Day of Silence marking the Hindu New Year, observed with fasting, meditation, and silence.

cultural_events.name: Waisak
cultural_events.writeup: Buddhist festival celebrating the birth, enlightenment, and death of Buddha, prominently observed at Borobudur.

cultural_events.name: Jakarta Fair
cultural_events.writeup: Annual event showcasing Indonesian culture, trade, and entertainment, held in the capital city.

cultural_events.name: Toraja Funeral Ceremony
cultural_events.writeup: Traditional elaborate funeral rites in South Sulawesi involving rituals, dances, and buffalo sacrifices.

cultural_events.name: Pasola Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional spear-fighting festival held by the Sumba people to celebrate the rice-planting season.

food_writeup: Indonesian cuisine is diverse, featuring rice as a staple accompanied by dishes like nasi goreng (fried rice), satay (grilled skewered meat), rendang (spicy beef stew), and sambal (chili paste). It reflects a blend of indigenous, Indian, Chinese, and European influences.
brief_history: Indonesia has a rich history influenced by Hindu-Buddhist kingdoms, Islamic sultanates, and European colonialism, particularly Dutch rule. It declared independence in 1945 and has since developed into the world's largest archipelagic state and a major emerging economy.

important_people.name: Sukarno
important_people.description: First President and founding father of Indonesia

important_people.name: Suharto
important_people.description: Second President who led for over three decades

important_people.name: Joko Widodo
important_people.description: Current President known for infrastructure development

current_conflicts: Indonesia faces internal challenges including separatist movements in Papua, religious and ethnic tensions in some regions, and environmental issues related to deforestation and resource management.
